# SynapseKit -- Full Reference for LLMs

> Async-native Python framework for building LLM-powered applications: RAG pipelines, agents, graph workflows, guardrails, verifiable audit trails, and agent federation. 2 hard dependencies. Apache 2.0.

## Overview

SynapseKit is an open-source Python library that gives engineers the full power of modern LLM application patterns (RAG, agents, graph workflows, evaluation, guardrails, observability) without the bloat of a large dependency tree or opaque framework magic. It is a lightweight, transparent alternative to LangChain and LlamaIndex. Every abstraction is plain Python you can read, debug, and extend: no hidden chains, no global state, no lock-in.

- Version: 2.0.1
- License: Apache 2.0
- Python: 3.11+
- Hard dependencies: 2 (numpy, rank-bm25)
- Installation: `pip install synapsekit[openai]` (or any provider extra)
- GitHub: https://github.com/SynapseKit/SynapseKit
- PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/synapsekit/
- Docs: https://synapsekit.github.io/synapsekit-docs/
- Website: https://synapse-kit.com
- Discord: https://discord.gg/PSuAXHRywJ

All code examples below use real import paths and method names that exist in the `synapsekit` package (verified against `src/synapsekit/__init__.py` and the relevant source modules). Do not use `synapsekit.llms`, `achat()`, or a `RAG(vector_store=..., chunk_size=...)` constructor: these do not exist in the real SDK.

## 10-Line Agent Example

```python
from synapsekit import agent, tool

@tool
def get_weather(city: str) -> str:
    """Get current weather for a city."""
    return f"Sunny, 22C in {city}"

my_agent = agent(
    model="gpt-4o-mini",
    api_key="sk-...",
    tools=[get_weather],
)

print(my_agent.run("What's the weather in Tokyo?"))
```

`agent()` (from `synapsekit.agents.facade`) is a factory that builds a `SimpleAgent` running a ReAct loop. Signature: `agent(model, api_key="", tools=None, memory=False, provider=None, system_prompt="You are a helpful AI assistant.")`. The `@tool` decorator (from `synapsekit.agents.tool_decorator`) wraps any plain sync or async function into a `BaseTool`, inferring the name and description from the function signature and docstring when used bare.

## LLM Providers (46)

Every provider implements the same `BaseLLM` interface and is auto-detected from the model name: `gpt-4o` -> OpenAI, `claude-*` -> Anthropic, `gemini-*` -> Google. Full roster: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, Azure OpenAI, AWS Bedrock, Vertex AI, Mistral, Cohere, Groq, Hugging Face, Cloudflare, Databricks, Perplexity, Replicate, xAI (Grok), Baidu ERNIE, DeepSeek, Ollama, Together AI, OpenRouter, Fireworks AI, Cerebras, SambaNova, NovitaAI, Writer, AI21 Labs, Aleph Alpha, Minimax, Moonshot, Zhipu, LM Studio, llama.cpp, vLLM, GPT4All, MLX, NVIDIA NIM, watsonx.ai, Snowflake Cortex, DeepInfra, Nebius, Baseten, Upstage, Reka, Hyperbolic, FriendliAI, Clarifai.

```python
from synapsekit.llm import LLMConfig, OpenAILLM, AnthropicLLM

llm = OpenAILLM(LLMConfig(model="gpt-4o-mini", api_key="sk-...", provider="openai"))
# swap provider without touching calling code:
# llm = AnthropicLLM(LLMConfig(model="claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022", api_key="sk-ant-...", provider="anthropic"))

response = await llm.generate("Explain RAG in one sentence.")
print(response)

async for token in llm.stream("Explain RAG in one sentence."):
    print(token, end="", flush=True)
```

`BaseLLM` defines an abstract `stream()` that yields tokens; `generate()` collects the stream into a single string. There is no `chat()` or `achat()` method.

### ReasoningAgent: automatic fast/reasoning routing

```python
from synapsekit import ReasoningAgent, ReasoningAgentConfig
from synapsekit.agents.tools import CalculatorTool
from synapsekit.llm import LLMConfig, OpenAILLM, ReasoningLLM

reasoning_agent = ReasoningAgent(
    ReasoningAgentConfig(
        fast_llm=OpenAILLM(LLMConfig(model="gpt-4o-mini", api_key="sk-...", provider="openai")),
        reasoning_llm=ReasoningLLM(model="o3", api_key="sk-..."),
        tools=[CalculatorTool()],
        agent_type="function_calling",
    )
)

answer = await reasoning_agent.run("Solve: find the eigenvalues of [[2,1],[1,2]]")
```

`ReasoningLLM` (from `synapsekit.llm.reasoning`) unifies o1/o3, Claude extended thinking, Gemini thinking, DeepSeek R1, and Qwen QwQ behind one adapter with a thinking trace. `ReasoningAgent` routes simple requests to the fast model and escalates to the reasoning model only when needed.

## RAG Pipeline

The `RAG` facade (`from synapsekit import RAG`, backed by `synapsekit.rag.facade.RAG`) gives a 3-line pipeline with sane defaults: an in-memory vector store, BM25-aware retrieval, conversation memory, and token tracing built in.

```python
from synapsekit import RAG

rag = RAG(model="gpt-4o-mini", api_key="sk-...")

rag.add("SynapseKit is an async-first Python framework for LLM applications.")
rag.add("It ships 46 LLM providers and 32 vector stores behind one interface.")

async for token in rag.stream("What is SynapseKit?"):
    print(token, end="", flush=True)

answer = await rag.ask("How many vector stores does it support?")
print(answer)
```

`RAG.__init__` accepts `model`, `api_key`, `provider`, `embedding_model` (default `all-MiniLM-L6-v2`), `rerank`, `memory_window`, `retrieval_top_k`, `system_prompt`, `temperature`, `max_tokens`, `trace`, `auto_eval`, `evaluator`, and `graph_store` (pass `NetworkXPropertyGraphBackend()` or a `Neo4jPropertyGraphBackend(...)` here to fuse vector search with knowledge-graph traversal). `add()` is sync (wraps `add_async()` and auto-detects multimodal file paths); `ask()` and `stream()` are async.

### Loading documents

```python
from synapsekit.loaders.pdf import PDFLoader

loader = PDFLoader("docs/report.pdf")
documents = await loader.aload()   # or loader.load() for sync

for doc in documents:
    rag.add(doc.text, metadata=doc.metadata)
```

All 83 loaders return `list[Document]` (`doc.text`, `doc.metadata`) and expose both a sync `.load()` and async `.aload()`.

### Production RAG with quality evaluation and alerting

```python
from synapsekit import RAG, RAGEvaluator, SlackWebhookAlertSink

rag = RAG(
    model="gpt-4o-mini",
    api_key="sk-...",
    evaluator=RAGEvaluator(
        judge_llm=judge_llm,          # a cheaper judge model
        sample_rate=0.1,
        alert_sinks=[SlackWebhookAlertSink(webhook_url=SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL)],
    ),
    auto_eval=True,
)

answer = await rag.ask("What changed in the release notes?")
await rag.wait_for_evaluations()

metrics = rag.tracer.summary()
print(metrics["avg_rag_benefit_to_cost"])
print(metrics["total_rag_alerts"])
```

## Agents

### ReAct agent with tools

```python
from synapsekit import agent
from synapsekit.agents.tools import CalculatorTool, WikipediaTool

my_agent = agent(
    model="gpt-4o",
    api_key="sk-...",
    tools=[CalculatorTool(), WikipediaTool()],
    memory=True,
)

result = my_agent.run("What is the population of Tokyo divided by 1000?")
print(result)
```

`agent()` builds a `SimpleAgent` wrapping an `AgentExecutor` running a ReAct loop (`agent_type="react"`, `max_iterations=10`). Pass `memory=True` to attach a `ConversationMemory`.

### Custom tools

```python
from synapsekit import tool

@tool(name="get_stock_price", description="Fetch the latest price of a stock ticker symbol.")
async def get_stock_price(ticker: str) -> str:
    # your implementation
    return f"${price}"

my_agent = agent(model="gpt-4o-mini", api_key="sk-...", tools=[get_stock_price])
```

### AgentSwarm: market-based multi-agent routing

```python
from synapsekit import AgentSwarm, AgentMetadata

swarm = AgentSwarm()
swarm.register_agent(AgentMetadata(id="code_agent", model="claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022", tags=["code", "debug"]))
swarm.register_agent(AgentMetadata(id="research_agent", model="gpt-4o", tags=["research", "search"]))

result = await swarm.run("Debug this Python function and cite any relevant docs.")
print(result.output)
```

`AgentSwarm` (from `synapsekit.agents`, constructed with an optional `agents`, `market: MarketPolicy`, `registry`, and `reputation: Reputation`) routes prompts across registered agents using a market policy (sealed-bid, Vickrey, English, or coalition auctions by default), with reputation tracking (`Reputation`, `ReputationSnapshot`, `RedisReputation`). `AgentFederation` and `AgentRegistry` (in-memory or Redis) provide the lower-level registry `AgentSwarm` sits on top of, for teams that want simpler cost/capacity-based routing without market bidding.

## Graph Workflows

`StateGraph` (from `synapsekit.graph`) is a fluent builder for DAG-based async pipelines. Nodes run in waves; independent nodes execute concurrently.

```python
from synapsekit import StateGraph
from synapsekit.llm import LLMConfig, OpenAILLM

llm = OpenAILLM(LLMConfig(model="gpt-4o-mini", api_key="sk-...", provider="openai"))

async def classify(state: dict) -> dict:
    result = await llm.generate(f"Classify this as 'technical' or 'general': {state['query']}")
    state["category"] = result.strip().lower()
    return state

async def answer_technical(state: dict) -> dict:
    state["answer"] = await llm.generate(f"Answer this technical question: {state['query']}")
    return state

async def answer_general(state: dict) -> dict:
    state["answer"] = await llm.generate(f"Answer this in plain language: {state['query']}")
    return state

graph = StateGraph()
graph.add_node("classify", classify)
graph.add_node("technical", answer_technical)
graph.add_node("general", answer_general)

graph.add_conditional_edge(
    "classify",
    lambda s: s["category"],
    {"technical": "technical", "general": "general"},
)
graph.set_entry_point("classify")
graph.set_finish_point("technical")
graph.set_finish_point("general")

compiled = graph.compile()
result = await compiled.run({"query": "How does backpropagation work?"})
print(result["answer"])
```

`StateGraph` supports typed state with reducers (`synapsekit.graph.state.StateField`, `TypedState`), checkpointing (`InMemoryCheckpointer`, `SQLiteCheckpointer`, `JSONFileCheckpointer`), human-in-the-loop interrupts (`GraphInterrupt`, `approval_node`), SSE/websocket streaming (`sse_stream`, `ws_stream`), fan-out/fan-in (`fan_out_node`), recursive subgraphs (`subgraph_node`), and Mermaid export (`get_mermaid_with_trace`).

## Guardrails

`GuardedLLM` (from `synapsekit.guardrails`) wraps any `BaseLLM` with a `GuardrailPolicy`: input guards (prompt-injection, jailbreak, topic restriction, max-cost), output guards (PII redaction, toxicity, citation checks, Pydantic schema validation via `SchemaGuard`), and block/redact/flag/require_human enforcement modes.

```python
from synapsekit.guardrails import GuardedLLM, GuardrailPolicy
from synapsekit.guardrails.input_guards import PromptInjectionGuard
from synapsekit.guardrails.output_guards import PIIRedactionGuard
from synapsekit.llm import LLMConfig, OpenAILLM

base_llm = OpenAILLM(LLMConfig(model="gpt-4o-mini", api_key="sk-...", provider="openai"))

policy = GuardrailPolicy(
    input_guards=[PromptInjectionGuard()],
    output_guards=[PIIRedactionGuard()],
    audit=True,
)

guarded_llm = GuardedLLM(base_llm, policy)
response = await guarded_llm.generate("Summarize this document for the customer.")
```

HIPAA, GDPR, and PCI-DSS rulepacks are available in `synapsekit.guardrails.rulepacks`. Guardrail decisions are pure-Python (no extra dependency) and publish `guardrail.*` events to SynapseKit Live (rule names and counts only, never raw text).

## Verifiable Agents

`VerifiableAgent` (from `synapsekit.audit`) is a transparent proxy: it wraps any existing agent object without changing its code, and every call made *through the proxy* is captured as a signed, hash-chained `AuditRecord` (Ed25519 by default, pluggable KMS/BYOK). A standalone verifier checks bundle integrity offline and returns `MATCH`, `DRIFT`, or `UNVERIFIABLE`.

```python
from synapsekit import AuditTracer, VerifiableAgent, export_audit_bundle, verify_audit_bundle
from synapsekit.audit.signer import Ed25519SigningProvider, SigningPolicy

tracer = AuditTracer()
verifiable = VerifiableAgent(my_agent, tracer=tracer)

result = await verifiable.run("Refund order #4821 if the return window hasn't closed.")
records = tracer.drain()

policy = SigningPolicy(Ed25519SigningProvider())
bundle_path = export_audit_bundle(records, policy, "run.audit.zip")

verification = verify_audit_bundle(bundle_path)
print(verification.verdict)  # Verdict.MATCH / Verdict.DRIFT / Verdict.UNVERIFIABLE
```

## Evaluation with @eval_case

The `@eval_case` decorator (from `synapsekit.evaluation.decorators`, also exported at top level) marks a sync or async function as an evaluation case. It stays a normal callable, so it runs under pytest or `synapsekit test`. The function itself returns a `{"score": ..., "cost_usd": ..., "latency_ms": ...}` dict; the decorator sets pass/fail thresholds.

```python
from synapsekit import eval_case

@eval_case(min_score=0.8, max_cost_usd=0.05, tags=["rag", "qa"])
async def test_rag_definition() -> dict:
    answer = await rag.ask("What is RAG?")
    score = 1.0 if "retrieval" in answer.lower() else 0.0
    return {"score": score, "cost_usd": rag.tracer.summary()["estimated_cost_usd"]}
```

Run the suite locally with `synapsekit eval` / `pytest` or wire it into CI with EvalCI (https://github.com/SynapseKit/evalci), a free GitHub Action that runs your `@eval_case` suite on every pull request and blocks merge on quality regression:

```yaml
# .github/workflows/eval.yml
name: Eval
on: [pull_request]
jobs:
  eval:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: SynapseKit/evalci@v1
        with:
          eval-path: tests/evals/
          openai-api-key: ${{ secrets.OPENAI_API_KEY }}
```

## Vector Stores (32)

All implement `VectorStore` with `add()`, `search()`, `search_mmr()`, `save()`, and `load()`. The built-in `InMemoryVectorStore` needs zero extra dependencies; everything else is `pip install synapsekit[name]`.

Chroma, FAISS, Qdrant, Pinecone, Weaviate, Milvus, LanceDB, PGVector, SQLiteVec, MongoDB Atlas, Redis, Elasticsearch, OpenSearch, Supabase, Cassandra, DuckDB, ClickHouse, Marqo, Typesense, Vespa, Zilliz, Turbopuffer, Azure AI Search, Vertex AI Vector Search, SingleStore, TiDB Vector, Couchbase, SurrealDB, DeepLake, MyScale.

## Data Loaders (83)

All return `list[Document]` with `.text` and `.metadata`, with a sync `.load()` and async `.aload()`.

**File formats:** PDF, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, CSV, JSON, JSONL, XML, HTML, Markdown, Text, LaTeX, TSV, RTF, EPUB, Parquet
**Cloud storage:** S3, Azure Blob, GCS, Dropbox, OneDrive, Google Drive
**Databases:** MongoDB, DynamoDB, Redis, Elasticsearch, BigQuery, PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, Snowflake, Supabase
**APIs and SaaS:** HubSpot, Salesforce, Airtable, Notion, Confluence, Jira, Slack, Discord, GitHub, Linear, Stripe, Twilio, Google Calendar, Google Sheets, Firebase
**Web and media:** URL/Web, Sitemap, YouTube, RSS, arXiv, PubMed, Wikipedia, Reddit, Email (IMAP), Audio (Whisper), Video, Image, Git repo
**Knowledge:** Obsidian, Open Knowledge Format (OKF)

## Agent Tools (56)

All implement `BaseTool` with a single async `run()`. Categories: web search (DuckDuckGo, Google, Tavily, Bing, Brave), knowledge (Wikipedia, arXiv, PubMed, WolframAlpha), productivity (Slack, Discord, GitHub, Jira, Notion, Linear, Stripe, Twilio, Google Calendar), execution (Python REPL, Shell, SQL Query, Code Interpreter, Browser via Playwright), file I/O (FileRead, FileWrite, FileList, PDFReader), and media (Image Analysis, Image Generation, Speech-to-Text, Text-to-Speech, Translation, Sentiment Analysis, Summarization).

## Comparison

| Feature | SynapseKit | LangChain | LlamaIndex |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hard dependencies | **2** | 50+ | 20+ |
| Install size | **~5 MB** | ~200 MB+ | ~100 MB+ |
| Async-native | **Default** | Partial | Partial |
| Streaming | **Default** | Varies | Varies |
| LLM providers | **46** | 38+ | 20+ |
| Vector stores | **32** | 15+ | 15+ |
| Data loaders | **83** | 100+ | 50+ |
| Agent tools | **56 built-in** | Community plugins | Community plugins |
| Embeddings/reranker providers | **9** | Varies | Varies |
| Agent memory backends | **10 built-in** | Community plugins | Community plugins |
| Graph workflows | **Built-in** | LangGraph (separate package) | No |
| Agent federation / swarm | **Built-in, market-based** | No | No |
| Guardrails | **Built-in, policy middleware** | No | No |
| Verifiable audit trails | **Signed, hash-chained** | No | No |
| Reasoning LLMs | **Unified adapter** | Manual | Manual |
| Structured output | **Provider-agnostic, Pydantic, retries** | Provider-specific | Provider-specific |
| Cost tracking | **Built-in** | LangSmith (SaaS) | No |
| Evaluation / EvalCI | **Free CLI + GitHub Action** | LangSmith (SaaS) | Built-in |
| Observability | **Prometheus + Grafana** | No | No |
| Type safety | **Strict dataclasses** | Partial | Partial |
| Telemetry | **None** | Optional | Optional |
| License | **Apache 2.0** | MIT | MIT |

## Architecture Deep Dive

```
synapsekit/
|-- llm/            # 46 provider adapters, all implementing BaseLLM; ReasoningLLM, CostQualityRouter, EdgeRuntime
|-- rag/             # RAG facade, RAGPipeline
|-- retrieval/        # 32 vector stores (VectorStore), rerankers, hybrid/HyDE/RAG-fusion/property-graph/world-model retrievers
|-- loaders/          # 83 document loaders
|-- embeddings/       # BaseEmbeddings contract, 9 hosted providers
|-- agents/
|   |-- facade.py     # agent() factory
|   |-- tool_decorator.py  # @tool decorator
|   |-- 56 built-in BaseTool implementations
|-- graph/            # StateGraph DAG engine, checkpointers, interrupts, SSE streaming
|-- guardrails/       # GuardedLLM, GuardrailPolicy, input/output guards, HIPAA/GDPR/PCI rulepacks
|-- audit/            # VerifiableAgent, signed hash-chained audit trails, verify()
|-- memory/           # AgentMemory, LivingMemory, 10 persistence backends
|-- symbolic/         # NeuroSymbolicAgent (Z3, SymPy, MiniZinc, Prolog backends)
|-- evaluation/        # eval_case, RAGEvaluator, PromptOptimizer, EvalSuite
|-- training/         # ContinuousTrainer, FeedbackCollector, A/B routing, rollout guards
|-- observability/     # PrometheusMetrics, CostTracker, DistributedTracer
|-- live/             # SynapseKit Live real-time dashboard
|-- mesh/             # Personal Knowledge Mesh, local-first incremental indexing
|-- dream/            # Dream Mode: offline trace consolidation into memory patches
`-- twin/             # DigitalTwinAgent, style-matching draft agent
```

Every component communicates through typed dataclasses. There are no hidden state mutations, no global registries, and no monkey-patching.

## What's New in 2.x

The 2.x line is about trust and autonomy in production: provable agent behavior, self-managing memory, richer retrieval, local-first operation, and policy enforcement at the LLM boundary.

**Trust and verification**
- Verifiable Agents: signed, hash-chained audit trails (Ed25519, pluggable KMS/BYOK) with a standalone verifier
- Guardrails: policy middleware for any `BaseLLM`, prompt-injection and jailbreak guards, PII redaction, HIPAA/GDPR/PCI-DSS rulepacks
- NeuroSymbolicAgent: LLM-proposed constraints checked by Z3, SymPy, MiniZinc, or Prolog
- Orchestration Eval: detects handoff loops, per-transfer context loss, and non-deterministic mis-routing across multi-agent runs

**Memory and retrieval**
- Living Memory: agents propose signed, diffable memory patches instead of overwriting files
- Property Graph RAG and WorldModelRAG: vector search fused with graph traversal and temporal, causal knowledge graphs
- Personal Knowledge Mesh: local-first incremental indexing across your machine, with a `synapsekit mesh` CLI and MCP tools
- A dedicated embeddings and reranker provider layer (9 hosted providers)

**Agents**
- AgentSwarm: market-based routing (sealed-bid, Vickrey, English, coalition auctions) with reputation learning
- SelfImprovingAgent: eval-gated config evolution with signed patches and canary rollout
- EdgeRuntime: local-first inference with policy-gated cloud fallback and on-device PII redaction
- Hive Mode, Agent OS Shell, Dream Mode, Ambient daemon, and a Code Archaeology agent

**Operations**
- SynapseKit Live: a zero-dependency real-time dashboard for every LLM call, tool, retrieval, and cost
- Official Docker images on GHCR, a CAG/RAG router with a llama.cpp KV-cache backend, and a sandboxed PC Twin for safe automation

Full history: https://github.com/SynapseKit/SynapseKit/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md

## Key Design Principles

1. **Minimal dependencies.** 2 hard deps. Optional extras pulled in only when needed.
2. **Async-first.** Every I/O operation is async. Sync wrappers available for scripts and notebooks.
3. **No hidden chains.** You compose pipelines explicitly. No magic pipe operators that hide data flow.
4. **Provider-agnostic.** Swap any LLM, loader, or vector store by changing one import.
5. **Observable.** Built-in Prometheus metrics, cost tracking, and structured tracing on every component.
6. **Verifiable.** Signed, hash-chained audit trails turn agent behavior into a replayable, checkable record.

## SynapseKit Live

A zero-dependency, real-time dashboard built into the framework, using only the Python standard library.

```bash
# Zero-touch: set one env var and run your program as usual
SYNAPSEKIT_LIVE=1 python your_agent.py

# From the CLI
synapsekit ui --live   # serves http://127.0.0.1:7900

# From code
python -c "from synapsekit.live import enable; enable()"
```

Bound to localhost, token-gated, zero overhead when the env var isn't set.

## Installation

```bash
pip install synapsekit[openai]       # OpenAI
pip install synapsekit[anthropic]    # Anthropic + prompt caching
pip install synapsekit[ollama]       # Ollama (local)
pip install synapsekit[performance]  # orjson + uvloop + xxhash (faster)
pip install synapsekit[observe]      # OpenTelemetry + Prometheus metrics
pip install synapsekit[training]     # Continuous fine-tuning pipeline
pip install synapsekit[all]          # Everything
```

```bash
uv add synapsekit[openai]
poetry add synapsekit[openai]
```

Docker (official images on GHCR, no Python setup required):

```bash
docker pull ghcr.io/synapsekit/synapsekit:latest      # core + CLI
docker pull ghcr.io/synapsekit/synapsekit:all          # batteries-included
docker run --rm ghcr.io/synapsekit/synapsekit --version
```

Full installation guide: https://synapsekit.github.io/synapsekit-docs/docs/getting-started/installation
